question: Will the Kennedy Center's main building be open to the general public on October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is closed: main building physically shut and fenced since 2026-09-16, ~16 days before the question date. The closure mechanic is a 7-day safety closure with weekly reevaluation controlled by management that has already voted a 2-year closure through 2028 and publicly tied reopening to the name dispute at the D.C. Circuit; Oct 2 falls inside a probable extension window. Reference class of announced one-week emergency safety closures of major US public buildings with documented structural failure reopens within ~2.5 weeks maybe 30% of the time; adverse operator incentives, damage located in the Grand Foyer (the main entry), and October programming already gutted by the cancellation wave push well below that. The live YES paths are (a) Judge Cooper finding the Sept 23 status report pretextual and ordering reopening with compliance before Oct 2 - he has so far been deferential and denied an emergency hearing, and DOJ appeals everything - or (b) a face-saving partial reopening, which the fine print would count. No market prices this event; the only nearby contracts are thin demolition-announcement markets (Polymarket 0.11 by Oct 31) whose threshold, deadline and criterion all differ, so evidence not anchor. Evidence is one-sided toward closure but the pivotal filing has not yet occurred, so I stay above a pure status-quo floor.
calls.reference_class: Announced short-term (~1 week) emergency safety closures of major US public/cultural buildings following documented structural failure, where the operator has separately announced a multi-year closure and is under adversarial litigation - fraction admitting the public again within ~2.5 weeks
